original_question: Conjecture: The derived length of a finite solvable group G does not exceed |Cod(G)| − 1. The Fitting height of G is known to be at most min{|Cod(G)|−1, |Cod(G)|/2+1} (G. Qian, Y. Zeng, J. Group Theory, to appear).
target_in_paper: Open problem 21.109 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)"
correct_elements: Your draft matches Problem 21.109 essentially verbatim: it has the right class of groups (finite solvable groups), the exact conjectured bound on derived length, and the same contextual sentence about the known Fitting-height bound.
missing_details: The notation Cod(G) is not defined in the draft. In the paper, Cod(G) is the set of irreducible character codegrees of G.
The underlying characters are irreducible complex characters χ of G.
Each codegree is defined by cod(χ)=|G:ker χ|/χ(1).
To be fully stand-alone, it should be explicit that Cod(G) is a set, so its cardinality |Cod(G)| does not count multiplicities.
If full self-containment is desired, one should write dl(G) for the derived length, or explicitly say 'the derived length of G'.
The Fitting-height sentence is background/motivation recorded with the problem; it is not part of the conjecture itself.
refined_question: Let G be a finite solvable group. For each irreducible complex character χ of G, define its codegree by cod(χ)=|G:ker χ|/χ(1), and let Cod(G)={cod(χ): χ∈Irr(G)} be the set of irreducible character codegrees of G. Is it always true that the derived length dl(G) satisfies dl(G)≤|Cod(G)|−1? (As background, the paper notes that the Fitting height of G is known to be at most min{|Cod(G)|−1, |Cod(G)|/2+1}.)
justification: Within arXiv:1401.0300, your draft is not approximating a neighboring result: it is exactly the open conjecture stated as Problem 21.109. The only paper-faithful additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the definitions of cod(χ) and Cod(G), which are supplied earlier in 20.78 and restated by reference in 21.108. Since the paper gives no equivalent reformulation of 21.109, the sharpest refinement is simply the same conjecture with the notation expanded and no extra hypotheses added.
